audit.notes: Read .ctor (3, Skill 2, Uncommon 3, Self 1), get_CanonicalVars BlockVar(15, ValueProp 8), EnergyVar(1), OnUpgrade Block +5 only, get_GainsBlock true, <OnPlay>b__5_0 (Type == Attack 1), <OnPlay>d__5::MoveNext: TriggerAnim Cast; CreatureCmd.GainBlock(owner creature, Block, cardPlay); Hand(2) cards Where Attack ToList; foreach: if !EnergyCost.CostsX -> EnergyCost.AddUntilPlayed(-Energy.IntValue, false). No keywords override, no ExtraHoverTips. Extract diff old->new confirms the change: CalculationBase 15 (+1), CalculationExtra 5 (+3), CalculatedBlockVar, GetPowerAmount<StrengthPower> removed (the old max(0, Strength) clamp itself was not re-read; old IL not dumped). Also read CardEnergyCost (--dump-any) and LocalCostModifier: AddUntilPlayed(-1, false) adds LocalCostModifier(-1, Relative 2, expiration WhenPlayed 4, IsReduceOnly false); it is removed only by AfterCardPlayedCleanup (WhenPlayed) or end of combat, NOT at end of turn, so the reduction persists across turns/discard until the card is played -> duration 'until_played' is right. A 0-cost Attack CANNOT go below 0: GetWithModifiers ends with Math.Max(0, cost) and GetResolved / GetAmountToSpend also take Math.Max(0, ...); X-cost and negative-base (unplayable) cards return early unmodified (and are filtered anyway). Side note: the -1 modifier is still stored on a 0-cost card and modifiers are summed before the final clamp, so it can cancel a later relative +1 increase on that card. Open question about going below 0 can be closed: no. Fingerprint matches extract.

audit.notes: Read v0.113.1 IL: ctor CardModel(0, Attack, Uncommon 3, AnyEnemy 2); CanonicalVars DamageVar(8, ValueProp 8); OnUpgrade Damage +3; <OnPlay>d__3::MoveNext ThrowIfNull(cardPlay.Target); AttackCommand.CreateContextAsync; results = CreatureCmd.Damage(ctx, cardPlay.Target, Damage.BaseValue, ValueProp 8, card, cardPlay).ToList(); AddHit; r = FirstOrDefault; if r != null: others = CombatState.GetTeammatesOf(r.Receiver).Except([cardPlay.Target]).Where(b__3_0 IsHittable).ToList(); if Count > 0: CreatureCmd.Damage(ctx, others, r.TotalDamage + r.OverkillDamage, ValueProp 8, owner creature, card, cardPlay, ModifyDamageHookType 8). Numbers, targets and order agree with the entry. What I dispute is the description of the change. (1) 'per-hit damage caps now apply to it' is not supported: Hook.ModifyDamageInternal applies ModifyDamageCap only when the hook type has flag 8, and every CreatureCmd.Damage overload without an explicit hook type forwards ModifyDamageHookType 14 (All) (read <Damage>d__4/d__6/d__9), while the only cap hooks (IntangiblePower, HardToKillPower ModifyDamageCap) never look at ValueProp, so caps already applied to the old Unpowered splash; the old IL is not on disk, so this is the most likely reading, not a proven one. (2) The real gameplay change is missed: ValuePropExtensions.IsPoweredAttack = HasFlag(Move) && !HasFlag(Unpowered). Old props 12 (Move|Unpowered) made the splash a non-powered hit; new props 8 make it a powered attack. Its amount is still only cap-modified (hook type Cap skips additive/multiplicative, so Strength/Vulnerable still do not raise it), but every reaction keyed on IsPoweredAttack now fires per splashed enemy, e.g. ThornsPower.BeforeDamageReceived (enemy Thorns hits back), EnvenomPower.AfterDamageGiven (Poison on each splashed enemy), and the other 60+ models that call IsPoweredAttack (CurlUp, FlameBarrier, PainfulStabs...). Fields I would write: keep effects as they are, but extend the second effect's amount_from with '; the splash is a powered attack (ValueProp Move, IsPoweredAttack true since v0.113.1), so on-attack reactions such as Thorns, Curl Up and the owner's Envenom trigger for each splashed enemy'; replace the v0.113.1 evidence line with 'v0.113.1 re-review: changed (minor). Splash ValueProp 12 (Move|Unpowered) -> 8 (Move) with explicit ModifyDamageHookType 8 (Cap): amount still only cap-modified, but the splash now counts as a powered attack for on-attack hooks'; and drop 'now' from the caps wording in the open question. Fingerprint equals current extract. | Developer ruling 2026-11-16: the reviewer is right, and the v0.113.1 patch notes say the same (effects triggered by attack damage, such as Reaper Form and Envenom, now also trigger on Omnislice's second damage): the change is that the splash counts as a powered attack; damage caps are not new.

RandomBranchState.GetStateWeight: UseOnlyOnce -> 0 once the state is in StateLog (each rat calls for backup at most once); cooldown N -> 0 if the state is among the last N logged move states; the result is multiplied by the weight lambda.

The remove [Monster, Elite] field is exactly what the IL does. Settled the Elite question by reading the caller: RunManager.RollRoomTypeFor(Unknown) -> UnknownMapPointOdds.Roll (--dump-any UnknownMapPointOdds). The set passed to Hook.ModifyUnknownMapPointRoomTypes is _nonEventOdds.Keys (Monster, Elite, Treasure, Shop) + Event, minus the caller's excluded types, so Elite IS in the set, but its odds are -1 (ctor sets Monster 0.1, Elite -1, Treasure 0.02, Shop 0.03) and Roll skips any type with odds < 0; the unrolled-type increase adds the base odds (-1) so Elite stays negative. The only code that makes Elite rollable is the DeadlyEvents run modifier (scan of all IL for set_EliteOdds / SetBaseOdds callers: DeadlyEvents.AfterRunCreated sets EliteOdds 0.1 and base 0.1, AfterRunLoaded base 0.1), and that same AfterRunCreated removes JuzuBracelet from every player's RelicGrabBag and the SharedRelicGrabBag. So in normal play the added Elite removal has no effect; it only matters if Juzu is obtained some other way in a Deadly Events run. Also seen: on a profile's first run (UnlockState.NumberOfRuns == 0) Roll forces the first two Unknown points to Event and the third to Monster before the hook is called, so Juzu does not stop that Monster. Suggest (not required) recording both facts in evidence/open_questions in place of the unread-caller open question. fingerprint equals the current extract record.
